Modern commercial solar panels routinely achieve 20% to 26% efficiency, led by mainstream TOPCon (22.5–24.5%) and premium HJT (23–25%) technologies, while perovskite-silicon tandem cells represent the cutting edge with lab records reaching 34.85% (`solar_research.md`) and early pilot commercial efficiencies of 26–28.5% (`solar_report.md`). Following a team standup, the finalized report successfully balances commercial buyers' needs by anchoring the executive dashboard in ROI metrics—such as payback periods of 4.2 to 5.5 years—while retaining a robust technical breakdown of emerging tandem architectures for technology strategists (`meeting_decision.md`, `solar_report.md`).

However, the research artifact (`solar_research.md`) and the final report (`solar_report.md`) are both truncated mid-sentence, cutting off the remaining text in the sources and conclusion sections respectively. Consequently, the final synthesis lacks the full citation list and the complete concluding outlook outlined in the agreed report structure.
